overview: Sri Sanghi Temple, officially Sanghi Temple Devasthanam, is situated atop the picturesque hillock of Paramananda Giri in Sanghi Nagar, Ranga Reddy district, Telangana, approximately 35 km from Hyderabad. Visitors are welcomed by a grand Maha Dwaram and a towering Raja Gopuram visible from several kilometers away. An outstanding example of Chola-Chalukya architecture in pristine white marble, designed by Padma Shri sculptor Sri Ganapathy Sthapathy, the temple was built by the Sanghi family and inaugurated in 1991. Dedicated to Lord Venkateswara, the complex houses numerous shrines and is one of the most visited spiritual destinations in Telangana, drawing lakhs of devotees annually.
summary: Sri Sanghi Temple, atop Paramananda Giri in Sanghi Nagar, Ranga Reddy district, Telangana (~35 km from Hyderabad), is a Chola-Chalukya style temple complex in white marble dedicated to Lord Venkateswara. Built by the Sanghi family with the blessings of Jagadguru Sri Jayendra Saraswathi Shankaracharya of Kanchipuram and designed by Padma Shri sculptor Sri Ganapathy Sthapathy, it was constructed in 18 months and inaugurated in 1991. The complex features a towering Raja Gopuram, a Maha Dwaram, shrines to Padmavathi, Ashtalakshmi, Shiva-Kamalambika, Rama-Sita-Lakshmana-Hanuman, Vijayaganapathi, Kartikeya, Durga, Navagrahas and Hanuman, plus a Pavitra Vanam and Kalyana Mandapam. It sees exceptional footfall on Ekadashi and New Year's Day.

history.content: The origins of Sanghi Temple date back to 1990, when the Sanghi family envisioned creating a magnificent spiritual centre. With the blessings of Jagadguru Sri Jayendra Saraswathi Shankaracharya of Kanchipuram and under the guidance of Shri Ram Sharan Sanghi and Smt. Kamala Rani Sanghi, the project was spearheaded by Shri Ravi Sanghi and Smt. Anita Sanghi. Construction commenced in 1990 and was completed in just 18 months, culminating in the inauguration of the temple in 1991. Since then it has become one of the most visited spiritual destinations in Telangana, attracting lakhs of devotees annually.
legends: Built with the blessings of Jagadguru Sri Jayendra Saraswathi Shankaracharya of Kanchipuram.

sthala_puranam: Built by the Sanghi family in 1991, modeled after Tirumala Balaji Temple. The presiding deity Lord Venkateswara's idol is ~9.5 ft tall, similar to Tirumala. The temple complex also houses shrines for Padmavathi, Rama, Hanuman, Shiva, Durga, Ganesh, Kartikeya, and Ashtalakshmi.
religious_significance: Sanghi Temple is regarded as a symbol of faith, unity and devotion. Built as a spiritual sanctuary amidst nature, it has become an epitome of belief among devotees, who visit seeking blessings, inner peace and spiritual solace while admiring its architectural grandeur.
spiritual_significance: The temple witnesses exceptionally high footfall during Ekadashi, New Year's Day, and major Hindu festivals. Pilgrims visit seeking blessings, inner peace and spiritual solace.
healing_beliefs: Blessings, inner peace and spiritual solace through worship
miracles_and_devotee_experiences: Devotees believe prayers here bring prosperity, health, and fulfillment of wishes. The temple is especially crowded on Ekadashi and New Year's Day, with devotees reporting peace and blessings akin to Tirumala darshan.
architecture: An outstanding example of Chola-Chalukya architecture designed by renowned sculptor and Padma Shri awardee Sri Ganapathy Sthapathy. The complex is constructed predominantly from pristine white marble and features intricate carvings depicting Hindu mythology and divine beings. Three majestic Gopurams — dedicated to Lord Venkateswara, Goddess Parvathi and Lord Shiva — adorn the foothills of Paramananda Giri. A long flight of steps leads visitors to the complex through an ornately carved entrance, in a style that seamlessly blends South Indian and Dravidian influences.

top_reviews: Tripadvisor (rimjhim, 2/5, 'Not at all maintained!'): 'We went to Sanghi Temple yesterday as a part of a family outing. The timings on the internet were mentioned as 8:30 to 10:30 AM and 4 PM to 6 PM so we rushed to reach there on time in the evening. The road to the temple is quite nice. It doesn't feel as if you are in Hyderabad as there is greenery on both sides. The entrance hoarding to the temple showed different timings. Its open in the evenings from 4 PM TO 8 PM contrary to what is mentioned on the web and on Sundays it is open from 8AM to 8PM. The temple is not well maintained at all. The grass and greenery that was there a few years back is no longer there. There were muddy patches everywhere and very little of grass. No floral plants as seen a few years back. So the only so called beauty is in terms of the temple structure. The priests seemed highly reluctant to do any kind of 'free' service like offering teertham, flowers etc. It was a major put off. We stayed there till 5:30pm and there was no light in the sanctum sanctorum which was dark inside and made it difficult to see the idols. Very demotivated temple staff. The temple has quite some numbers of monkeys around which are a nuisance. They kept coming near us when we were seated on the benches, forcing us to leave the seats. Overall it was a disappointment. The only plus point was the weather. There's no point driving to the outskirts of the city to see a barren temple land and priests who are highly demotivated!'

Tripadvisor (anilk3243, 4/5, 'Sanghi'): 'Located in sangi nagar beautiful peaceful temple. Main embodiment is Lord venkateswara. 25 km away from Hyderabad city, Sanghi temple. One of the hyderabad's sight seeing places. Even appeared in various Telugu movies. There exists pavitra vanam with beautiful flowers in that garden. Temple also has a Kalyana Mandapam where marriages are performed. In night times the temple looks spectacular.'

Tripadvisor (ganeshks112, 5/5, 'Peaceful place Sangi Temple'): 'Sangi Temple is one of the Excellent religious attraction in Hyderabad. The temple is quiet peaceful. This is the lord Venkateswara Temple located at top of the hill. There are 10 temples in the compound. It is a beautiful temple. Own vehicles are suitable for this place. The temple is very nice with cool environment.'

Tripadvisor (KASIRAO5646, 4/5, 'Sanghi Temple- A place to visit'): 'Sanghi Temple, located at Sanghi Nagar is about 35 km from Hyderabad city. It is in Koheda Village about 8 Kms from the National Highway between Hyderabad and Vijayawada. The sacred Raja Gopuram, which is very tall, can be seen from several kilometers away. The temple complex is located on the top of Paramanand Giri hill, which attracts a number of devotees who seek the Gods' blessings. The beauty of the slope around the temple is a popular view among its visitors. There are many small temples in the complex but the main temple is Lord Venkateswara. The idol of Venkateshwara inside the sanctum sanctorum is 9-½ ft tall. Timings of Sanghi Temple for public is from 08.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon and from 4.00 p.m.to 8.00 pm. This temple is considered to be a main attraction of Hyderabad.'

introduction.en: Sri Sanghi Temple, atop Paramananda Giri in Sanghi Nagar, Ranga Reddy district, Telangana, about thirty-five kilometres from Hyderabad, is a Chola-Chalukya style temple complex in white marble dedicated to Lord Venkateswara. Welcomed by a grand Maha Dwaram and a towering Raja Gopuram, it was built by the Sanghi family and inaugurated in 1991, designed by Padma Shri sculptor Sri Ganapathy Sthapathy. The complex houses shrines to Padmavathi, Ashtalakshmi, Shiva-Kamalambika, Rama, Vijayaganapathi, Kartikeya, Durga and the Navagrahas, and draws lakhs of devotees annually.

history.en: The Sanghi family envisioned the temple in 1990. With the blessings of Jagadguru Sri Jayendra Saraswathi Shankaracharya of Kanchipuram, and under the guidance of Shri Ram Sharan Sanghi and Smt. Kamala Rani Sanghi, Shri Ravi Sanghi and Smt. travel_guide.en: Sanghi Temple is about thirty-five kilometres from Hyderabad, a sixty to ninety minute drive. The nearest airport is Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, twenty-eight to thirty-eight kilometres away. The nearest railway stations are Ghatkesar, about thirteen kilometres, and Secunderabad, about thirty-four kilometres. Sanghi Nagar Bus Stop is about one kilometre from the temple. The temple is open Monday to Saturday from 8:00 AM to 1:00 PM and 4:00 PM to 8:00 PM, and 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM on Sundays, holidays and festivals.

faq.question: Where is Sanghi Temple located?
faq.answer: Sanghi Temple is atop Paramananda Giri in Sanghi Nagar, Ranga Reddy district, Telangana, approximately 35 km from Hyderabad.

faq.question: Which deity is worshipped at Sanghi Temple?
faq.answer: The presiding deity is Lord Venkateswara (Balaji), whose ~9.5-foot idol is modeled after the deity at Tirumala. The complex also houses shrines to Padmavathi, Ashtalakshmi, Shiva-Kamalambika, Rama, Vijayaganapathi, Kartikeya, Durga, Navagrahas and Hanuman.

faq.question: What are the temple timings?
faq.answer: Monday–Saturday: 8:00 AM–1:00 PM and 4:00 PM–8:00 PM. Sundays, public holidays and festival days: 8:00 AM–8:00 PM.

faq.question: When was Sanghi Temple built?
faq.answer: Construction began in 1990 and the temple was inaugurated in 1991, completed in 18 months by the Sanghi family.

faq.question: Who designed Sanghi Temple's architecture?
faq.answer: The temple was designed by renowned sculptor and Padma Shri awardee Sri Ganapathy Sthapathy in the Chola-Chalukya style.

faq.question: How far is Sanghi Temple from Hyderabad?
faq.answer: Approximately 35 km, about a 60–90 minute drive depending on traffic.

faq.question: How can I reach Sanghi Temple?
faq.answer: By air via Rajiv Gandhi International Airport (~28–38 km), by rail via Secunderabad (~34 km) or Ghatkesar (~13 km) stations, or by road via Sanghi Nagar Bus Stop (~1 km) / Hayathnagar Bus Station (~15 km).

faq.question: What are the major festivals at Sanghi Temple?
faq.answer: Sri Krishna Janmashtami, Ganesh Chaturthi, Durga Ashtami, Maha Navami, Vijayadashami, Deepavali, Ekadashi celebrations and New Year Special Darshan, with exceptional footfall on Ekadashi and New Year's Day.

faq.question: What is the Raja Gopuram at Sanghi Temple?
faq.answer: It is the temple's towering ornamental entrance tower, visible from several kilometers away, serving as an iconic landmark of the complex.

faq.question: What facilities are available at Sanghi Temple?
faq.answer: Drinking water, pooja item shops, a Kalyana Mandapam, a Pavitra Vanam (Holy Garden) and open parking. Nearby restaurants and restrooms are limited, so plan accordingly.
